processes.description: A desk member updates the deals and splits spreadsheet for the month and sends it round to the desk with a short cover note. The note says what changed or what was left out this time and asks readers to come back with questions. People also ask for related reports, such as an industrial report that a colleague built before he left. When the person who keeps the spreadsheet moves on, someone else takes it over.
steps: Gather the month's deals and splits from the desk's records.
Update the monthly spreadsheet and note anything not yet added.
Send the updated spreadsheet to the desk with a short cover note.
Answer readers' questions and correct the sheet where needed.
Hand the spreadsheet or report to a new owner when the keeper leaves or changes role.

stalls.summary: The spreadsheet and related reports depend on whoever built them. A report built by a colleague who has left has to be asked for, and the spreadsheet is expected to pass from one person to another, with no sign of written steps for the next owner.

automation.approach: Generate the monthly deals and splits sheet from the deal capture system with a saved query or report, so that each month's update becomes a refresh and a review rather than a rebuild. Write down how the spreadsheet and the industrial report are built and where their data comes from, so a new owner can pick them up.
automation.rationale: The quotes show a routine monthly update whose main risk is handover: reports are tied to the people who built them, and ownership changes hands. A written procedure keeps the work going when people leave, and it is also the starting point for automating the data pull.

work_estimate.rationale: Most of the minutes go to pulling the month's deals and splits, entering them into the spreadsheet and checking totals before sending. The quotes show a routine update with little rework, so the estimate is under an hour. Most of the data pull and layout could come from a report, but someone still has to review the sheet and decide what to leave out.

processes.description: Assistants and coordinators pass on the facilities team's move schedule, such as a move into the new building or a move set for a weekend, and forward the packing and labelling instructions to their group. Staff pack and label their boxes and ask for a convenient time to be moved. After moves, an assistant is asked to clear out all unoccupied desks in the Central Region.
steps: Receive the move date and the new seating plan from facilities.
Forward the packing and labelling instructions to the group.
Staff pack and label their boxes before the move.
Collect staff requests about move timing and pass them on.
Clear out unoccupied desks that are left behind.

automation.approach: Keep a standard move checklist covering packing, labelling, timing requests and desk clear-out. Send it with every move notice and collect timing requests through one form or reply, instead of forwarding instructions again for each group.
automation.rationale: Each round repeats the same instructions: pack, label, pick a time, clear vacated desks. A checklist sent with the move notice saves forwarding and re-explaining. The physical work of packing and clearing desks still needs people.

work_estimate.rationale: The minutes go to packing and labelling boxes, arranging move times with the movers and clearing out vacated desks. One mover has only a couple of boxes, but a regional desk clear-out takes longer, so the range is wide. Only the scheduling and instruction steps could be handled by a tool. The physical packing and clearing stays manual.

processes.description: A desk accountant reports the origination recognized in the nightly run, broken down by desk, and tells originators when their credit has or has not shown up. He traces individual originators' deals, codes all origination, including Denver's, to a single cost centre, and books corrections in a later month so the quarter's gas P&L is right. When an originator's group asks for data on its deals, he sets up a daily origination report for them.
steps: Run the nightly origination recognition and note the totals by desk.
Tell the originators and their groups what origination was recognized.
Compare recognized origination with the schedule and flag differences.
Trace missing originations for individual originators.
Code origination to the agreed cost centre.
Book corrections in a later month to fix the quarter's P&L.
Send deal data and a daily origination report to the groups that ask for them.

stalls.summary: Originations that do not appear where expected have to be traced by hand for a named originator.
Mistakes surface after the books close and are fixed with corrections in a later month to set the quarter's gas P&L right, which means rework.
Origination credit depends on someone else booking it, and the originator is told to wait for the entry to appear that night.

contradictions.summary: The two sides' figures disagree: one party has recognized an amount of origination that the desk accountant does not see on his side, so the two sets of records have to be reconciled.

automation.approach: Build a daily reconciliation report that compares origination recognized in the books with the origination schedule by originator, desk and cost centre. It would flag missing, mismatched or miscoded entries before close, and the same output would go to the groups that want a daily origination report.
automation.rationale: The quotes show a single accountant tracing missing originations, explaining mismatched figures and booking late corrections. A standard reconciliation layout makes differences visible every day instead of after the quarter's P&L is affected, and it is also the report the groups ask for.
